evidence.text: The page lists oracle-bone examples, bronze inscriptions, Warring States forms, received Shuowen forms, Qin forms, clerical script and later regular script, with some identified by artifact or corpus references. Its prose asserts that later forms follow the oracle form and offers a thumb interpretation, but this is the site's analysis rather than a settled identification. It provides a source lead for period-labelled forms, not an independently verified continuous graphic lineage.

gaps: The source pages substantiate three candidate identities, provenance and reuse statements, but none of the image pixels were visually inspected.
The web preview requests failed with cache misses. The repository acquisition attempt reports a separate SVG document-type/entities parsing error; no converted image was sourced or tested.
The bronze candidate has no specific archaeological object or absolute date on its Commons page. The seal candidate represents the received Shuowen seal-script style, not an excavated seal.

Guoxuedashi provides period-labelled examples and its own thumb interpretation, but that interpretation is disputed in the supplied dossier; the labels alone do not establish every stroke transition or a continuous lineage. No candidate should be described as an artifact photograph.

limitations.text: The three candidates have verified Commons description pages, direct original-file links, source identifiers and stated reuse provenance. The preview fetches failed and the repository acquisition attempt reports an SVG parsing limitation, so pixel availability to the harness remains unresolved. No visual inspection is claimed.

The oracle and bronze candidates are modern redrawings in script styles, not photographs of artifacts. The bronze page does not supply a specific object or absolute date, while the seal candidate represents the received Shuowen form rather than an excavated seal.
